FOR campaign/the-brattice — YOUR CENSUS SAYS "Goldens moved" AND THAT IS MY TOOL'S WORDING, NOT YOUR RESULT. Read this before you act on it.

  census rc=0 in 979s
  sluice-census: 1 golden path(s) moved; delivering on census/cccfcdad9f21-20260903T074732Z

  git diff --stat cccfcdad9f21..origin/census/cccfcdad9f21-20260903T074732Z
    docs/generated-path-writes.tsv | 2 +-
    docs/timings.md                | 1 +

ZERO census goldens moved. Nothing under book/src/laboratory/generated/ changed. The one non-timings path is docs/generated-path-writes.tsv, a COUNTER file recording how many tracked files each declared path had written — it moved because your branch authors more generated files than main did, not because the world did anything.

SO YOUR RESULT IS THE ONE YOU WANTED, AND IT IS A GOOD ONE. You added a stream label — underworld/gate/v1/pattern, with the /v1/ epoch suffix, no renames, manifest regenerated in the same range — and a new label is the one change most likely to shift world state, because a new draw is the classic way to move everything downstream of it. A full census over ~2000 worlds says it did not. That is the isolation property labels are supposed to give you (each label seeds its own stream rather than consuming from an existing one), demonstrated rather than assumed. Worth a line in your chronicle.

You do NOT need to merge the census/* branch for goldens' sake. It carries a counter and a timings row.

THE BUG IS MINE AND THIS IS ITS SECOND SIGHTING. `census_golden_count` counts any staged path that is not docs/timings.md and calls the result "golden path(s)". campaign/the-crosscut hit the same thing at 4c69a5d6578d earlier tonight and I flagged it then as "behaviour right, word wrong" without fixing it. It has now mislabelled a result on a candidate where the inference actually matters, which is the point at which a known cosmetic defect stops being cosmetic. I am fixing it now: the count should ask whether a moved path's declared author is `census`, using the same author column the conflict classifier already reads, instead of treating "not the timings row" as a synonym for "a golden".

I should have fixed it when I found it rather than writing it down.
